warnings: CRITICAL: CO2 treatment is UNREPLICATED - only one chamber per CO2 level. Authors explicitly acknowledge this: 'a fundamental problem with the experimental design is that the CO2 treatment was unreplicated and hence the responses of the seedlings to CO2 are potentially confounded by any chamber effects.' This means there are no true independent replicates at the chamber level.
Factorial design: Species (2) x Soil type (2: basalt vs rhyolite) x CO2 (2: ambient vs elevated) - must be extracted separately for each combination.
Data are presented in FIGURES (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2) not tables - numerical values must be read from bar graphs with error bars.
Phenolic and condensed tannin data reported on FRESH WEIGHT basis, while nitrogen and mineral nutrients reported on DRY WEIGHT basis - units differ between outcome variables.
Leaf toughness values are reported as toughness DIVIDED BY leaf thickness (corrected for thickness) - not raw toughness.
Some mineral nutrients (P, K, Ca) showed CO2 effects in Flindersia but NOT in Alphitonia - species-specific responses must be noted.
Some outcomes (toughness, total phenolics in Alphitonia) showed soil-type-dependent CO2 effects - soil type is a moderating factor.
n=5 seedlings per subgroup after splitting into two groups of five for different analyses - very small sample size.
Seedlings were previously fertilized with slow-release NPK fertilizer in potting mix before transplanting to native soils - may affect baseline nutrient status.
The 790 ppm CO2 level is higher than the typical 550-700 ppm range used in most meta-analyses; this is approximately a doubling of ambient.

recon.extraction_guidance: 1) All data are in figures (bar graphs), not tables - require digitization of Fig. 1 (N, P, K, Ca, Na) and Fig. 2 (phenolics, tannins, thickness, toughness). 2) Extract separately for each of the 8 combinations: 2 species x 2 soils x 2 CO2 levels. 3) N and mineral data are on dry weight basis; phenolics/tannins on fresh weight basis - record units carefully. 4) Toughness is already corrected for thickness (toughness/thickness ratio). 5) The CO2 treatment is unreplicated (single chamber per level) - flag this as a major quality concern for meta-analysis inclusion. 6) Percentage changes reported in text can be used to verify digitized values: N declined 25% in Alphitonia, 29% in Flindersia; Na declined 44% in both; P/K/Ca declined 19-28% in Flindersia only; condensed tannins increased 29% in Flindersia only. 7) For the meta-analysis of mineral dilution effects, the primary outcomes are N, P, K, Ca, Na from Fig. 1. 8) Two-way ANOVA was used (CO2 x soil type as fixed factors) but CO2 was unreplicated - treat statistical outputs with caution.
